content.text:
The unit in Princes Pass is unit id 27, a footman. There's only one unit. Moving it out would lose Prince's Pass control (cannot leave power token, 0 power).

Options: move footman to Starfall or Yronwood to capture a castle without combat. That gains 1 castle area. But loses Princes Pass (a land area, 0 castle). Princes Pass has supply=1, crown=1. Losing it loses supply icon (currently 3 supply icons; dropping to 2 may affect supply track on next Supply card).

Actually capturing Starfall gives castle area +1. Is that worth losing Princes Pass? Victory is about castle areas. Starfall is castle=1 -> counts as 1 castle area. Currently Martell has 1 castle area (Sunspear stronghold). Moving footman to Starfall gains 1 → 2 castle areas. But leaving Princes Pass empty loses control since no power token. Wait, can we keep a unit in Princes Pass? Only one unit exists there. Single footman. Moving it out vacates.

Alternatively, we could move the footman to Starfall but... only one unit, can't split.

Hmm, but wait—do we want to also consider that the footman needs to stay to protect? Princes Pass is adjacent to dornish-marches (tyrell footman) and the-boneway (baratheon footman). Moving out of Princes Pass loses it.

Starfall is a castle=1 area, uncontested (controller null, no units). Capturing gains 1 castle area. Standing there with a single footman. Is Starfall safe? Starfall neighbours: east-summer-sea, princes-pass, salt-shore, west-summer-sea, yronwood.

Risk: after this round, someone could take Starfall. But a castle area is a castle area.

Also considering: capturing Yronwood (castle=1) also gains 1. Yronwood neighbours: princes-pass, salt-shore, sea-of-dorne, starfall, sunspear, the-boneway.

Which is better? Starfall vs Yronwood. Both castle=1. Yronwood is closer to our stronghold Sunspear and land-connected; Starfall requires... it's land, adjacent to princes-pass. Both adjacent to princes-pass.

Let me think about defensibility. Yronwood is adjacent to the-boneway (baratheon footman, March -1) and sea-of-dorne (our support ship). Our ship in sea-of-dorne gives support to Yronwood combat. Starfall is adjacent to west-summer-sea, east-summer-sea — enemy potential ships. Starfall only adjacent to our land areas princes-pass, salt-shore. Hmm.

Actually support: our sea-of-dorne ship supports battles in adjacent areas. sea-of-dorne adjacent areas: east-summer-sea, storms-end, sunspear, the-boneway, yronwood. So Yronwood is supportable by our ship. Starfall is not (west-summer-sea, east-summer-sea not our support).

Defensively, Yronwood is better. Also Yronwood has supply=... let's check: yronwood [land; castle=1] no supply. Starfall [land; castle=1; supply=1] has supply=1. Starfall gives supply icon.

Hmm, capturing Starfall gains a castle area + a supply icon. Capturing Yronwood gains castle area only.

But wait, does moving from Princes Pass to Starfall lose Princes Pass (supply=1, crown=1)? Net supply icons: lose 1 (Princes Pass), gain 1 (Starfall) = 0 net. For Yronwood: lose 1, gain 0 = -1.

Hmm. Alternatively, hold Princes Pass and don't move? But then no gain.

But we have 0 power. Losing Princes Pass means we lose crown icon too.

Let me think about the bigger strategic picture. Round 3. Martell at 1 VP. We want to grow. Capturing a castle with no combat is strong and free.

Actually wait — can we hold Princes Pass AND capture? Only one unit in Princes Pass. No.

Is there another Martell unit? Sunspear has knight (id 26) with Consolidate Power order. sea-of-dorne ship. That's it. So this march has only the one footman.

The key question: is gaining a castle worth losing Princes Pass? Yes, castle areas are the victory condition. We currently have 1 castle area (Sunspear). Gaining one → 2. That's meaningful.

But losing Princes Pass also loses a land area for tiebreaks and a supply/crown icon. Hmm.

Alternatively, could we move the footman and still preserve control by... no power tokens.

Hmm, wait. Actually, let me reconsider. Is Starfall truly empty and controllable? "Starfall (capture gains one castle area without combat)". Yes controller null.

Let's decide between Starfall and Yronwood. Consider future defense and support. Yronwood is supported by our ship in sea-of-dorne, and is central to our holdings (adjacent to Sunspear, salt-shore). Starfall is a bit isolated but has supply.

Actually consider the risk of the Baratheon footman in the-boneway marching into Yronwood? It has March -1 order. Baratheon could attack Yronwood. But that's their order this round maybe.

Given no power and limited units, I think capturing Starfall is slightly better due to the supply icon, but Yronwood is more defensible.

Hmm, but actually think: which castle can we more easily hold and which is more useful long-term? Both are peripheral. Starfall being adjacent to west-summer-sea (tyrell ship in redwyne-straights only) — Tyrell has a ship in redwyne-straights which is adjacent to west-summer-sea. Could be a threat.

Actually, let me reconsider holding Princes Pass. Princes Pass has crown=1 and supply=1. It's adjacent to Dornish Marches (Tyrell footman) and The Boneway (Baratheon footman). Currently we hold it with 1 footman.

Wait, but we could also move the footman to Yronwood or Starfall and NOT lose... no.

Hmm, what about moving to dornish-marches? That triggers combat with Tyrell footman. Our footman 1 + march +0 = 1. Tyrell defender 1 + any support? Actually dornish-marches has Consolidate Power order, no defense bonus. Combat would be our 1 vs their 1, tie broken by Fiefdoms: Tyrell is 1st, we're 3rd. Tyrell wins tie. Bad. Unless support. Our sea-of-dorne ship can't support dornish-marches. So no. Skip.

the-boneway: Baratheon footman with March -1. Attack: our 1 vs their 1, but they'd have -1 march modifier applied only if they're attacking, not defending. Defending, march modifier doesn't apply. So 1 vs 1, tie broken by Fiefdoms: Baratheon 4th, us 3rd → we win! Hmm, actually we could win and take The Boneway. But that's not a castle, just crown. And we'd lose Princes Pass. Not great.

So best options: Starfall or Yronwood (both free castle).

Let me weigh defensibility + supply. I'll pick Starfall for the supply icon? But strategically Yronwood may be better placed to consolidate our southern hold, and defensible with sea-of-dorne support.

Hmm, actually, wait. Let me reconsider: does Starfall connect to salt-shore? Yes: starfall [land; castle=1; supply=1]: east-summer-sea, princes-pass, salt-shore, west-summer-sea, yronwood. And salt-shore is ours (controlPowerToken martell). So Starfall is adjacent to our Salt Shore. Good, so we can reinforce from salt-shore? Salt shore empty.

Yronwood adjacent to sea-of-dorne (our ship, support) and sunspear.

I think for defense, Yronwood is better because our ship can support it. But Starfall gives supply. Let me check supply limits: we have supply track 2 → permitted army sizes 3,2,2. Our armies: Sunspear has knight (single unit, id 26) — single. Hmm actually select_units selected [25,28] at sunspear earlier, then observe shows sunspear only knight id 26? Let me re-read. Board: sunspear units: [{martell id 26 knight}]. Hmm, knight 26 only. sea-of-dorne ship id 24.

Population: single units. So supply not an issue.

Supply icons controlled: 3 (Princes Pass supply1, Salt Shore supply1, ... Sunspear supply1). Yes 3. If we lose Princes Pass and gain Starfall, still 3. If we gain Yronwood, 2.

Supply track adjustments happen on Supply card; losing one supply icon could drop us. Keeping 3 is safer.

Given victory is castle areas, both give +1 castle. Starfall also preserves supply count. I lean Starfall.

But wait: is there benefit to holding princes-pass? It has a crown icon (1) which matters for Game of Thrones (power) and Clash bidding? Crown icons matter for "Game of Thrones" Westeros card (gain power per crown) and Throne bids? Actually no, influence track bidding doesn't use crowns. Crowns used for Game of Thrones card power collection and for... Actually "Dark Wings Dark Words". Hmm.

We have 0 power, so gaining power matters. But Consolidate Power at Sunspear this round will give power (1 + power icons in Sunspear: crown 1... wait Sunspear has supply=1, crown=1; Consolidate Power gives 1 + number of Power icons. Power icons = crown icons? Actually "one Power token for each Power icon printed on the area". Sunspear crown=1 → 1 power icon. So sunspear consolidate gives 2 power.

OK. Losing Princes Pass crown icon loses future power generation.

Hmm, decision. Let me think about the actual best play. Honestly, capturing a castle without combat is strong and we should take it. Between Starfall and Yronwood...

Consider that we might later be able to hold both. But right now only one footman. Long-term, capturing Yronwood then later Starfall seems natural since they're adjacent to each other! Yronwood adjacent starfall. And princes-pass adjacent both.

Which to take first? If we take Starfall (supply), we lose Princes Pass. Then next round we could march from Sunspear/Salt Shore to Yronwood.

Actually, we lose Princes Pass either way (any move vacates it). Wait—unless the move destination is... no, moving out vacates.

Hold on: could we move the footman to Starfall, and Princes Pass becomes uncontrolled. Then an opponent could take Princes Pass freely. Dornish Marches Tyrell footman is adjacent. Meh.

Alternatively, keep the footman in Princes Pass and do nothing this march (empty moves list). Then no gain. Given we're behind at 1 VP, we should gain.

I'll go with capturing a castle. Which one?

Let me think about threat: Tyrell has 2 castles + 2 strongholds already (4 castle areas, VP 2? wait VP is 2 but 4 castle areas?). Hmm the strategicOverview says tyrell castles 2 strongholds 2 → 4 castle areas but victoryPoints 2. That's inconsistent... Oh wait, "castles" and "strongholds" might be counts. 2+2=4 castle areas, but VP shows 2. Hmm. Maybe they lost some? Actually victoryPoints field maybe counts differently. Let me recheck: baratheon castles 1 strongholds 1 landAreas 3 victoryPoints 1. Hmm 1+1=2 but VP 1. Martell castles 1 strongholds 1 → 2 but VP 1. Hmm.

Hmm, that's odd. Maybe VP = castle areas controlled? Martell controls Sunspear (stronghold, castle=2) — that's 1 castle area. And... does Martell control any castle=1? No. So Martell castle areas = 1. So "castles" count = 1? But listed castles 1 strongholds 1. Hmm maybe castles field counts both? For martell castles:1, strongholds:1. But controlledRegions: sunspear only castle region. So strongholds:1 = Sunspear, castles:1 = ??? Maybe they count the number of... hmm.

Actually maybe "castles" and "strongholds" are counts of controlled regions with those types, and Martell has 1 stronghold (Sunspear) and 0 castles → but shows 1. Inconsistent. Let me not rely.

Anyway VP target is castle areas. Martell 1, others mostly 2.

OK let me just decide: I'll move the footman to Starfall. Actually wait, let me reconsider defensibility more carefully since losing a unit to a counterattack would be bad.

Starfall: adjacent land areas princes-pass (ours, becoming empty), salt-shore (ours, empty), yronwood (neutral empty). Sea areas: east-summer-sea (has enemies? current: none listed, but Baratheon controls... east-summer-sea not in board list, so empty), west-summer-sea (empty). Threat of attack: Tyrell ship in redwyne-straights → adjacent to west-summer-sea, and highgarden/oldtown land. Tyrell could march ships to west-summer-sea and then transport to Starfall. But next round.

Yronwood: adjacent the-boneway (Baratheon footman), princes-pass, salt-shore, sunspear, starfall, sea-of-dorne (our ship). More exposed to Baratheon footman.

Given Baratheon footman in the-boneway with March -1... they might attack Yronwood? Actually their march is already revealed this round; they may have used it or will use it. The Boneway march -1 could be used to attack Prince's Pass or Yronwood or Dornish Marches. Hmm. If we take Yronwood, we'd be adjacent to their footman.

Starfall seems safer (fewer adjacent enemy land units; only reachable via ships or through our own areas).

I'll go Starfall.

Wait, but is Starfall reachable directly from Princes Pass? actionGuidance lists starfall as reachable. Yes.

Also note: moving to Starfall, does combat trigger? "triggersCombat": false, controller null. Good.

So final: moves = [{destination_region_id: "starfall", unit_ids: [27]}].

Hmm but schema for UnitMove only has destination_region_id, no unit_ids field! The schema says items: {destination_region_id}. Interesting—no unit_ids. So the harness determines units? Actually the schema maxItems 1 and only destination. Hmm. The description says "Destination groups and moving unit IDs" but the property schema lacks unit_ids. Possibly the tool infers we move all units, or unit selection handled elsewhere. Given only one unit (footman 27) in Princes Pass, moving the destination implies moving that unit. Actually wait—maybe there are hidden constraints. But since only one unit in Princes Pass, moving all = the footman.

Hmm, but if I only specify destination, perhaps all units move. That's fine (only one unit).

Actually careful: could there be more units? Board shows princes-pass units: [{martell id27 footman}]. Just one.

So submit {"moves":[{"destination_region_id":"starfall"}]}.

Hmm, but wait, let me reconsider whether moving out of Princes Pass is wise. Alternative: don't move (empty list) — preserves Princes Pass but no gain. Since we can't leave power token, we lose it. But gaining a castle is worth more than a supply/crown land area? In this game, castle areas are THE win condition. Yes, definitely take the castle.

Let me double check the concern about losing Princes Pass supply: our supply icons drop from 3 to... Princes Pass supply=1, Starfall supply=1. Net 0. Actually we keep 3. Fine.

Crown icons: lose 1. Meh.

OK go with Starfall.

Actually, let me reconsider once more between Starfall and Yronwood considering future expansion. If we take Starfall, then Yronwood remains neutral and easily taken later from Salt Shore or Sunspear or Starfall. If we take Yronwood, Starfall remains reachable from Princes Pass? No, Princes Pass now empty/uncontrolled. From salt-shore (adjacent starfall) though. Salt shore empty; we'd need to march a unit there.

Either fine.

One more consideration: Tyrell's ship in redwyne-straights and their holdings near Starfall? Starfall is adjacent to west-summer-sea. Redwyne-straights adjacent to west-summer-sea. Tyrell could contest. But Yronwood also could be contested by Baratheon.

I'll commit to Starfall. Let me maybe quickly check neighbors of starfall to confirm no surprises? The tool would help. Let me do check_neighbours on starfall.

Actually the observation already lists starfall's units and it's empty. But checking neighbours confirms current owners. Let me just do it to be safe. Then submit.

Let me also consider the option of moving to Yronwood. I'll check both maybe. Let's check starfall and yronwood.

moves.description: Destination groups and moving unit IDs. Unlisted units stay in the source. An empty list discards the order. Every group must be legal and fit Supply; an illegal final action is rejected without submitting the march.
moves.title: Moves

actionOutputSchema.title: resolve_march_args
actionOutputSchema.description: You are resolving one of your March orders. Choose which units move and their destinations. Units you omit remain in the source area; you may split an army across destinations, and a single unit can march on its own. An empty moves list removes this March order without moving anyone. Only one destination may start combat. Use the reachable destinations in actionGuidance and keep the resulting armies within Supply. Leaving a control token costs one available power token and preserves control of the source when you legally vacate it. Compare castles gained and lost, and count support around the destination battlefield before choosing an attack. Before attacking another army, use check_neighbours on that battlefield to verify the supporting areas. Your final answer resolves this one order; another remaining order is a later decision.
